"UNIX's missing `loop` command!"

loop lets you write powerful, intuitive looping one-liners in your shell. It provides easy-to-use options
for repeating commands with timers, counters, and stop conditions.

Usage (examples):

- Run a command repeatedly until interrupted:

    $ loop 'echo hello'

- Run a command every 5 seconds:

    $ loop --every 5s -- date

- Stop when output contains a value:

    $ loop --until-contains 200 -- ./get_response_code.sh --site example.com

- Iterate over a list from stdin:

    $ cat items.txt | loop -- 'echo $ITEM'

}

fn capture_file() -> (File, std::path::PathBuf) {
    let dir = env::temp_dir();
    let mut seed = SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|d| d.as_nanos() as u64)

    let name = rand_name(&mut seed);
    let path = dir.join(name);
    let capture = make_capture_file(&path).unwrap();
    (capture, path)
}

fn run(cfg: &Config) -> i32 {
    let mut items: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    if let Some(l) = &cfg.for_list {
        items.extend(l.iter().cloned());
    }
    if cfg.read_stdin || !std::io::IsTerminal::is_terminal(&std::io::stdin()) {
        let mut raw = Vec::new();
        let _ = std::io::Read::read_to_end(&mut std::io::stdin(), &mut raw);
        let buf = String::from_utf8_lossy(&raw).to_string();
        for line in buf.lines() {
            items.push(line.to_string());
        }
    }
    let mut item_idx = 0usize;
    let mut count: f64 = cfg.offset;
    let max_runs: i64 = match cfg.num {
        Some(n) => n,
        None => {
            if items.is_empty() {
                i64::MAX
            } else {
                items.len() as i64
            }
        }
    };
    let mut runs: i64 = 0;
    let mut first_output: Option<String> = None;
    let mut last_out: Option<String> = None;

    for n in nodes { emit_node(n, prog) }

fn emit_node(n: &Node, prog: &mut Vec<Inst>) {
    match n {
        Lit(c, ci) => prog.push(Char(*c, *ci)),
        Any => prog.push(Any),
        Class(cl) => prog.push(Class(cl.clone())),
        StartLine => prog.push(StartLine),
        ...
        Group(seq) => emit(seq, prog),
        Alt(branches) => {
            // chain of splits
            let mut jumps = Vec::new();
            for (i, b) in branches.iter().enumerate() {
                if i + 1 < branches.len() {
                    let split_pc = prog.len();
                    prog.push(Jmp(0)); // placeholder for Split
                    let body_start = prog.len();
                    emit(b, prog);
                    let jmp_pc = prog.len();
                    prog.push(Jmp(0));
                    jumps.push(jmp_pc);
                    let next = prog.len();
                    prog[split_pc] = Split(split_pc + 1, next);
                } else {
                    emit(b, prog);
                }
            }
            let end = prog.len();
            for j in jumps { prog[j] = Jmp(end); }
        }
        Rep{seq, min, max, greedy} => {
            // min copies
            for _ in 0..*min { emit(seq, prog); }
            match max {
                None => {
                    // star loop: Split(body, exit)
                    let split_pc = prog.len();
                    prog.push(Jmp(0));
                    let body_start = prog.len();
                    emit(seq, prog);
                    prog.push(Jmp(split_pc));
                    let exit = prog.len();
                    prog[split_pc] = Split(body_start, exit);
                }
                Some(m) => {
                    let extra = m - min;
                    // for each extra: Split(body, end)
                    let mut splits = Vec::new();
                    for _ in 0..extra {
                        let sp = prog.len();
                        prog.push(Jmp(0));
                        let bs = prog.len();
                        emit(seq, prog);
                        splits.push(sp);
                        // hmm, careful: each optional copy's split must point to the end
                    }
                    let end = prog.len();
                    for sp in splits { prog[sp] = Split(sp+1, end); }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

pub fn is_match(&self, text: &str) -> bool {
    let chars: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();
    let n = chars.len();
    let mut clist: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
    let mut on_clist = vec![false; prog.len()];
    let mut nlist = Vec::new();
    let mut on_nlist = vec![false; prog.len()];
    add_thread(&mut clist, &mut on_clist, 0, 0, &chars);
    for pos in 0..=n {
        // check for a match
        for &pc in &clist { if matches!(prog[pc], Inst::Match) { return true } }
        if pos == n { break }
        for &pc in &clist {
            match prog[pc] {
                Char(c, ci) => if chars[pos] == c || (ci && ci_eq(...)) { add_thread(nlist, ..., pc+1, pos+1, ...) },
                Class(cl) => if cl.matches(chars[pos], cl.ci) { add pc+1 },
                Any => if chars[pos] != '\n' { add pc+1 },
                AnyNl => add pc+1,
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        swap(clist, nlist); swap(on_clist, on_nlist); clear nlist;
    }
    false
}

fn add_thread(&self, list: &mut Vec<usize>, on: &mut Vec<bool>, pc: usize, pos: usize, chars: &[char]) {
    if on[pc] { return }
    on[pc] = true;
    list.push(pc);
    match self.prog[pc] {
        Inst::Jmp(x) => self.add_thread(list, on, x, pos, chars),
        Inst::Split(x, y) => { self.add_thread(list, on, x, pos, chars); self.add_thread(list, on, y, pos, chars) }
        Inst::StartLine => if pos == 0 { self.add_thread(list, on, pc+1, pos, chars) },
        Inst::EndLine => if pos == chars.len() { self.add_thread(list, on, pc+1, pos, chars) },
        Inst::StartText => if pos == 0 { ... },
        Inst::EndText => if pos == chars.len() { ... },
        Inst::WordB => if at_word_boundary(chars, pos) { add pc+1 },
        Inst::NotWordB => if !at_word_boundary(chars, pos) { add pc+1 },
        _ => {}
    }
}

fn closure(states, pos, text) -> Set:
    stack = states; visited = {}
    while let Some(pc) = stack.pop():
        if visited contains pc: continue
        visited.insert(pc)
        match prog[pc]:
            Jmp(x) → push x
            Split(x,y) → push x, push y
            Match → add to the "matched" flag
            StartLine → if pos == 0 → push pc+1

        Any => prog.push(Any),
        Class(cl) => prog.push(Class(cl.clone())),
        StartLine => prog.push(StartLine),

        Group(seq) => emit(seq, prog),
        Alt(branches) => {

            let mut jumps = Vec::new();
            for (i, b) in branches.iter().enumerate() {

                    let split_pc = prog.len();
                    prog.push(Jmp(0)); // placeholder for Split
                    let body_start = prog.len();
                    emit(b, prog);
                    let jmp_pc = prog.len();
                    prog.push(Jmp(0));
                    jumps.push(jmp_pc);
                    let next = prog.len();
                    prog[split_pc] = Split(split_pc + 1, next);
                } else {
                    emit(b, prog);
                }
            }
            let end = prog.len();
            for j in jumps { prog[j] = Jmp(end); }

fn emit_node(n: &Node, prog: &mut Vec<Inst>) {
    match n {
        Lit(c, ci) => prog.push(Char(*c, *ci)),
        Any => prog.push(Any),
        Class(cl) => prog.push(Class(cl.clone())),
        StartLine => prog.push(StartLine),
        ...
        Group(seq) => emit(seq, prog),
        Alt(branches) => {
            // chain of splits
            let mut jumps = Vec::new();
            for (i, b) in branches.iter().enumerate() {
                if i + 1 < branches.len() {
                    let split_pc = prog.len();
                    prog.push(Jmp(0)); // placeholder for Split
                    let body_start = prog.len();
                    emit(b, prog);
                    let jmp_pc = prog.len();
                    prog.push(Jmp(0));
                    jumps.push(jmp_pc);
                    let next = prog.len();
                    prog[split_pc] = Split(split_pc + 1, next);
                } else {
                    emit(b, prog);
                }
            }
            let end = prog.len();
            for j in jumps { prog[j] = Jmp(end); }
        }
        Rep{seq, min, max, greedy} => {
            // min copies
            for _ in 0..*min { emit(seq, prog); }
            match max {
                None => {
                    // star loop: Split(body, exit)
                    let split_pc = prog.len();
                    prog.push(Jmp(0));
                    let body_start = prog.len();
                    emit(seq, prog);
                    prog.push(Jmp(split_pc));
                    let exit = prog.len();
                    prog[split_pc] = Split(body_start, exit);
                }
                Some(m) => {
                    let extra = m - min;
                    // for each extra: Split(body, end)

    let chars: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();
    let n = chars.len();
    let mut clist: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
    let mut on_clist = vec![false; prog.len()];

                _ => {}
            }
        }

    }

}

fn add_thread(&self, list: &mut Vec<usize>, on: &mut Vec<bool>, pc: usize, pos: usize, chars: &[char]) {
    if on[pc] { return }
    on[pc] = true;
    list.push(pc);
    match self.prog[pc] {
        Inst::Jmp(x) => self.add_thread(list, on, x, pos, chars),
        Inst::Split(x, y) => { self.add_thread(list, on, x, pos, chars); self.add_thread(list, on, y, pos, chars) }
        Inst::StartLine => if pos == 0 { self.add_thread(list, on, pc+1, pos, chars) },
        Inst::EndLine => if pos == chars.len() { self.add_thread(list, on, pc+1, pos, chars) },
        Inst::StartText => if pos == 0 { ... },

        Inst::WordB => if at_word_boundary(chars, pos) { add pc+1 },
        Inst::NotWordB => if !at_word_boundary(chars, pos) { add pc+1 },
        _ => {}

  including the ANSI colouring when stderr is a tty (the suggestion itself is
  always green, exactly like clap 2).

* Env vars handed to the child: `ITEM` (from `--for` and/or stdin),
  `COUNT` (`offset + n*count-by`, printed with as many decimals as the
  `--count-by` *text* has) and `ACTUALCOUNT` (0 based iteration).
* stdin is slurped to EOF before the first run when `-i` is given or stdin is
  not a tty; the item list is `--for` values followed by stdin lines; when no
  `-n` is given the loop performs one iteration per item.
* Output of a run is printed line by line (`str::lines`, so CRLF pairs lose the
  CR and a run without output prints nothing); `--only-last` prints only the
  final run's output; `--summary` prints the `Total runs/Successes/Failures`
  tally.

  are applied per line, `-s`/`-f`/`-r` look at the exit status, `-t` compares
  the UTC clock before every run, `-d` measures the elapsed time.

  takes longer than the interval does not add extra delay and a run that fires
  a condition is not followed by a sleep.

  immediately (`$TMPDIR/.tmpXXXXXX`), the fd is shared and rewound before it is
  read back, so the two streams are interleaved exactly like the original.

  `called Result::unwrap() ...` at `src/main.rs:67:44`, and a broken stdout
  pipe panics inside the standard library â the line/column of the first two
  were matched by padding the source.

* The "compiled regex exceeds size limit" boundary is reproduced exactly for
  `a{n}` (327656/327657) and within a few instructions for `(a{2}){n}`, but the

  could not be observed exactly.

  exotic properties or scripts report `Unicode property not found` even when
  the real crate would accept them.

  may report either one â exactly like the original.

  parse as an integer simply never match, as observed.
* Duration parsing follows the observed grammar: digits/units separated by
  optional whitespace, `ns us ms s m h d w M y` and their long spellings, no
  fractional values, `u64` overflow reported as `number is too large`.
* Regex parsing covers the common syntax (classes, nested classes, POSIX
  classes, groups, named groups, inline flags, repetition, escapes, unicode
  properties).  Very unusual constructs (e.g. `(?P=...)`, set operations inside
  classes) may report a slightly different message than the real crate.

## Tests

```
./compile.sh
python3 tests/recorded.py    # CLI diagnostics, env vars, conditions, summary
python3 tests/clap.py        # argument parsing edge cases and repetition syntax
python3 tests/behaviour.py   # timings, stdin, temp dir, signals, regex-on-lines
```

**Reverse-engineered `loop` 0.6.1** (a Rust/clap CLI) purely by running the original binary, then reimplemented it from scratch in Rust with **no external crates** (custom clap-emulating parser, humantime-compatible duration parser, chrono-compatible UTC timestamp parser, and a regex engine written from scratch).

Key behaviours discovered and reproduced:
- Exact `--help`/`--version` text, usage line derived from `basename(argv[0])`
- All clap-2 diagnostics incl. "did you mean" (jaroâwinkler, optsâthenâflags order, lastâtieâwins) and ANSI colouring rules
- Child output captured through an **unlinked temp file** (`$TMPDIR/.tmpXXXXXX`) shared by stdout+stderr, printed lineâbyâline with `lines()` semantics
- `ITEM`/`COUNT`/`ACTUALCOUNT` env vars (COUNT formatted with as many decimals as the `--count-by` *text*)
- stdin slurped to EOF before the first run, `--for` list first then stdin lines, and one iteration per item when `-n` is absent
- Even spacing of runs (`start + n Ã-- every`), no trailing sleep when a condition fires
- All stop conditions (`-c -m -C -S -s -f -r -t -d -n`), `--summary` format, `-D` â exit 124, signalâkilled child â status 99
- Panic sites reproduced byteâforâbyte, including `src/main.rs:67:44` and `src/main.rs:123:45` (achieved by padding the source so the `.unwrap()`/`.expect()` calls land on the exact line/column)

A midâcourse incident: I accidentally overwrote the provided binary with my build, losing the reference â fortunately all expectations had already been recorded and are now encoded in `tests/` (all green).
